answer:
Political placement of Huesca, as each source names it:

Britannica places Huesca "in the kingdom of Granada" — the full entry reads: "HUESCA, one of the ancient and considerable towns of Spain, in the kingdom of Granada, situated on a plain in W. Long. 1..45, N. Lat. 32."[B:e1327-03]

Wikipedia places Huesca "within the autonomous community of Aragon," and adds that it "was the capital of the Kingdom of Aragon between 1096 and 1118," as well as capital of the eponymous Spanish province and of the comarca of Hoya de Huesca.[W:68298@1331057656]

So the two sources name different political entities: Britannica says the kingdom of Granada; Wikipedia says Aragon (autonomous community, and historically the Kingdom of Aragon).

Inference: the two sources disagree. Britannica's "kingdom of Granada" conflicts with Wikipedia's Aragon, which indicates one of them is erroneous; I cannot determine from these sources alone which is correct, since the Britannica text is taken as-is and its coordinates (N. Lat. 32) also do not match Huesca, Spain.
